summary: GitHub watches deduplicate unchanged check results across observations and restarts, distinguish Actions reruns by run and attempt, and label cancelled checks accurately.

replay.detail: No replay changes. Existing observation facts and persisted message subjects provide deduplication.

schema.detail: No new claim fields, tables, indexes or store version changes.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: Check wake identity uses the head, counted conclusion set and existing counted workflow (run ID, attempt) pairs, excluding readiness and suite metadata. Reruns with numeric workflow IDs can report a recurring conclusion. Checks without a numeric workflow run ID (external apps, or Actions runs whose databaseId is null) fall back to conclusions: a recurring identical result at the same head remains suppressed. This known limitation avoids new per-check identity fields. Existing messages remain readable. The existing required_checks.state can report cancelled; watches distinguish cancellation while github.event retains its checks-failed contract and cancelled required checks retain active refresh cadence. Optional checks remain excluded when required-check rules are available.

recovery.detail: An older build restores observation-based wake identity and treats cancellation as failure; previously delivered messages are retained.
